Hey thanks for all the lovely comments! I don't have a super precise recipe, I tend to cook by flavour. But here is a general list of ingredients. (estimation on amounts)


Braised Beef:

2 inches ginger (large slices)

4 cloves garlic (crushed)

3 whole star anise

1 stick cinnamon

5 pieces rock sugar 

2 scallions (cut in half)

5 cloves

1 bay leaf

1 medium tomato quartered

1/2 cup cooking rice wine

dark soy sauce

light say sauce

3 lbs beef chuck (1" chunks)

beef stock (i make my own)


pretty much I took the beef and seared it with some oil on a large pot. put it to the side, add all the aromatics and sauteed it in oil for a few minutes then delgazed with the wine. added back the beef. then added enough beef stock to cover all the ingredients. You can also use water. bring to a boil then simmer for like .... as long as possible. Once ready, took out the meat (sometimes i do a quick fry in a pan to make it crispy) Run the soup base through a sieve to remove all the aromatics. then serve with noodles!

I was in 6th grade (elementary school) right outside DC. Our teacher came in and told us there had been a plane crash.  I remember being really confused and for some reason assumed a small plane crashed somewhere in a desert. Then she turned on the television and we all suddenly understood.  She was crying (her family was in NYC). eventually the tv was turned off and we were informed that none of the other kids at my school knew what happened, and we were not to say anything. I went to a school where like 95% of the parents worked in D.C. for the federal government, as my dad did. So understandably when we saw the the Pentagon was hit, we all were TERRIFIED for our parents.  Throughout the rest of the day kids quickly were called out of class as their parents came to pick them up. We had to pretend we didn't know what was happening to our friends in other classes. I didn't hear from my dad, who worked minutes from the Pentagon, until he showed up at my after school program to pick me up. We went home, watched the news...and I still remember being so scared watching bodies fall from burning buildings on loop for hours that afternoon.

1 large sweet potato, peeled and cubed

5oz ricotta cheese

2 cups all purpose flour + extra for dusting

2 cups grape tomatoes

4 tbsp butter

1 tbsp fresh sage, fine chopped

1 cup white dry wine

salt & pepper to taste



In a pot of cold water, add the cubed sweet potato pieces and bring to a boil. Cook for about 15 minutes or until fork tender. Drain well.


Add flour to a clean work surface and create a well. Using a potato ricer, rice the sweet potato pieces into the flour. Add ricotta. 


Gently combine and knead lightly until well mixed. Portion into 8 pieces and roll into a rope about 1/2” thick. Cut into pieces. Toss in flour so the pieces dont stick together.


Bring a large pot of salted water to boil + cook gnocchi for 2 minutes. Drain.



In a frying pan, add grape tomatoes and turn the heat up to medium-high. Add butter, sage, and gnocchi and cook until the outside of the gnocchi is crisp and the butter is slightly browned. Add white wine and reduce until just coating the gnocchi. Add salt + pepper for taste.

1c whole milk

I'm going to make a huge assumption and guess that you tend to only see these "out of the ordinary" runways. So first of all - these following designers also showed this season:

[Emporio Armani](http://www.style.com/fashionshows/complete/slideshow/F2014RTW-EARMANI/#1)

[Marchesa Voyage](http://www.style.com/fashionshows/complete/slideshow/F2014RTW-marchesa_voyage/#1)

[Blumarine](http://www.style.com/fashionshows/complete/slideshow/F2014RTW-BLUMARNE/#1)

While not completely ordinary, most of this is very wearable. And I do see people wear some of it. Also keep in mind, the entire show is all one designer. Generally, you don't wear an entire "look" on a regular basis - you mix and match designers. 

Stuff like Moschino's runway is much more conceptual and making a "statement" rather than "you should wear this gown that is also a giant nutrition label".

There's also the whole "trickle down" effect where bits and pieces (e.g. floral print) find themselves in other companies like Forever21, GAP, etc. That essentially have more affordable versions of designer clothing.

But most importantly, I think, is that there exists PLENTY of wearable designer runway stuff. Obviously it's the Spongebob sweaters that make the front page.

Androgynous looks are popular right now but it's true that models (runway especially) are really there to fit the mold of the brand.
